guide.summary: Maya museums and archaeological sites, Hotel Zone dinners, beach-hotel breakfasts and sunset bars, and an Isla Mujeres reef park, checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan Museo Maya de Cancún for Tuesday to Sunday, since it is closed on Mondays, while Zona Arqueológica El Rey opens every day from 8:00 to 17:00.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Museo Maya de Cancún opens Tuesday to Sunday and is closed on Mondays, and Xoximilco Cancún runs Tuesday to Saturday only. Zona Arqueológica El Rey and El Meco open every day.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Your Museo Maya de Cancún ticket ($210 MXN for foreign visitors) also covers the San Miguelito archaeological zone. Puerto Madero Cancún takes reservations online, and Xoximilco gives online discounts when you book at least 7 days ahead.

toolkit.label: Last entry
toolkit.copy: Museo Maya de Cancún stops gallery entry at 17:00 and San Miguelito entry at 16:30. NIZUC Spa by ESPA asks you to arrive up to 90 minutes before a treatment and charges 100% for cancellations within 24 hours.

toolkit.label: Age and dress rules
toolkit.copy: Coco Bongo Cancún admits only over-18s with valid official ID and asks for smart casual dress. Xoximilco's minimum age is 5, NIZUC Spa treatments are for over-16s, and Fantino's dress code is smart casual.

guide.dek: Put the Maya sites on a weekday morning other than Monday, then book a Hotel Zone dinner ahead.
intro: This Cancún guide pairs Maya history with Hotel Zone dining, and every place in it was checked on its own website or on the public body that runs it. Museo Maya de Cancún, run by INAH at Km 16 of Boulevard Kukulcán, opens Tuesday to Sunday from 9:00 to 18:00, with last entry to the galleries at 17:00 and to the San Miguelito archaeological zone at 16:30. One ticket covers both: INAH lists $210 MXN for foreign visitors, with free entry if you are over 60 or under 13.

Two more INAH sites round out the history. Zona Arqueológica El Rey, at Km 18 of Boulevard Kukulcán, opens every day from 8:00 to 17:00, with general admission listed at $145 pesos. North of the city, El Meco sits at Km 2.7 of the road from Puerto Juárez to Punta Sam and opens daily from 08:00 to 16:30, with free entry on Sundays. For a day on Isla Mujeres, Garrafón Reef Natural Park's website lists Tuesday to Sunday opening, with boats from Playa Langosta in Cancún included in its packages.

Dinner in the Hotel Zone mostly faces the lagoon or the sea. Puerto Madero at Km 14.1 opens Monday to Sunday from 13:00 to 01:00 and asks you to book online. Fred's House at Km 14.5 opens daily from noon to midnight, and Ilios at Km 13.5 lists a 5:00 pm opening on its website. Downtown, La Habichuela on Calle Margaritas says it is open 365 days a year. At Kempinski Hotel Cancún, Casitas On The Beach serves dinner daily from 19:00, and the D-Lounge bar opens at 17:00 for sunset cocktails.

Evenings and mornings have their own rules. Coco Bongo at Km 9.5 admits only over-18s with valid official ID and asks for smart casual dress. Xoximilco, on the Cancún–Puerto Morelos highway, runs Tuesday to Saturday with check-in from 7:00 p.m. and a minimum age of 5. For a slower start, El Café Mexicano at the Kempinski serves breakfast every day from 7:00, and Café Antoinette's website lists 7am opening at its Xpuhil and Puerto Cancún branches. NIZUC Spa by ESPA opens daily from 9:00am to 9:00pm, with treatments for over-16s.
summaryCards: Start at Museo Maya de Cancún, open Tuesday to Sunday, where one ticket also covers the San Miguelito ruins, then add Zona Arqueológica El Rey, which opens every day.
Have breakfast at El Café Mexicano in Kempinski Hotel Cancún from 7:00, or at Café Antoinette on Calle Xpuhil, whose website lists a 7am opening.
Remember that Museo Maya de Cancún is closed on Mondays, Xoximilco runs Tuesday to Saturday, and Coco Bongo admits only over-18s with official ID.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites carry no 2026-dated content, so their hours are attributed to the website rather than stated as current: Lorenzillo's, La Habichuela, Ilios, Harry's, Garrafón, Señor Frog's (2023 group menu) and Café Antoinette (undated pages). Harry's lists hours that appear to be an error, and Fantino, KAYANTÁ Spa, Café de la Playa and Bar A-Kan publish no regular hours; NIZUC does not say whether non-guests can book its restaurants. RosaNegra's page could not be read, Ultramar's ferry sites refused or reset the connection, Xailing returned 403, and the Bisquets Obregón branch list did not load; none of these failures is evidence of closure. Ventura Park says it is closed indefinitely and The Club Grill is paused. Most named cafés, bakeries and taquerías in the original list had no official website.
